provenance.source: 34 CFR 300.320 (IEP contents), 300.321 (IEP team), 300.322 (parent participation), 300.323 (when IEPs must be in effect), 300.324 (development, review and revision)

items.title: Present levels of performance
items.text: The IEP states the student's present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum (for a preschool child, participation in appropriate activities).

items.title: Measurable annual goals
items.text: The IEP states measurable annual goals, academic and functional, that meet the needs resulting from the disability so the student can be involved in and progress in the general curriculum, and that meet each of the student's other disability-related educational needs.

items.title: Benchmarks for alternate assessment
items.text: For a student who takes alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, the IEP also describes benchmarks or short-term objectives.

items.title: How and when progress is reported
items.text: The IEP describes how progress toward each annual goal will be measured and when periodic reports on that progress will be given (for example quarterly, or with report cards).

items.title: Services, aids and supports
items.text: The IEP states the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services, based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, and the program modifications or supports for school personnel, that will let the student advance toward the goals, progress in the general curriculum, take part in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated with other students with and without disabilities.

items.title: Start date, frequency, location and duration
items.text: For each service and modification, the IEP gives the projected start date and the anticipated frequency, location and duration.

items.title: Participation with nondisabled peers
items.text: The IEP explains the extent, if any, to which the student will not take part with nondisabled students in the regular class and in extracurricular and nonacademic activities.

items.title: State and district assessments
items.text: The IEP lists individual accommodations needed on state and districtwide assessments; when the team decides on an alternate assessment, it states why the student cannot take the regular assessment and why the chosen alternate assessment is appropriate.

items.title: Transition services
items.text: Beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the student turns 16 (younger if the team decides), and updated each year, the IEP includes measurable postsecondary goals based on age-appropriate transition assessments for training, education, employment and, where appropriate, independent living, and the transition services, including courses of study, needed to reach them. States may set an earlier age.

items.title: Transfer of rights at the age of majority
items.text: Beginning at least one year before the student reaches the state's age of majority, the IEP states that the student has been told of the rights that will transfer at that age.

items.title: IEP team
items.text: The team includes the parents; at least one regular education teacher if the student is or may be in the regular environment; at least one special education teacher or provider; an agency representative who can provide or supervise specially designed instruction and knows the curriculum and resources; someone who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results; others with knowledge of the student at the parent's or agency's discretion; and the student when appropriate (always invited when transition is discussed).

items.title: Parent participation
items.text: The agency takes steps so that one or both parents attend or have the opportunity to take part: notice early enough, a mutually agreed time and place, other ways to take part when they cannot attend, an interpreter when needed, and a copy of the IEP at no cost. A meeting held without a parent requires records of the attempts to arrange one.

items.title: Initial IEP meeting
items.text: The meeting to develop the initial IEP is held within 30 days of the determination that the student needs special education and related services; services are made available as soon as possible after the IEP is developed.

items.title: IEP accessible to those who carry it out
items.text: Each teacher and provider responsible for carrying out the IEP can see it and is told of their specific responsibilities and the specific accommodations, modifications and supports it requires.

items.title: What the team considers
items.text: In developing the IEP the team considers the student's strengths, the parents' concerns for enhancing the student's education, the results of the initial or most recent evaluation, and the student's academic, developmental and functional needs.

items.title: Special factors
items.text: The team considers positive behavioral interventions and supports when behavior impedes the student's learning or that of others; the language needs of a student with limited English proficiency; Braille instruction for a student who is blind or visually impaired unless the evaluation shows it is not appropriate; the communication needs of every student, including language and communication mode for a student who is deaf or hard of hearing; and whether the student needs assistive technology devices and services.

items.title: Annual review
items.text: The team reviews the IEP periodically, and at least once a year, to decide whether the annual goals are being achieved, and revises it to address lack of expected progress, reevaluation results, information from or to the parents, anticipated needs or other matters.

items.title: Amending without a meeting
items.text: After the annual meeting, the parent and the agency may agree to change the IEP by a written amendment instead of a meeting; the team is told of the change and the parent receives a revised copy on request.
